# Bloomy v1.9.10
Action History now displays earnings to six decimal places, so small job payments and base rewards no longer round to $0.00. Stored amounts were already exact; no history is lost or changed.
For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

# Bloomy v1.9.9
A persistent Action History makes Bloomy's actions easier to understand.
- Open **Diagnostics → Action History** to search and filter actions, reported jobs, and base rewards. - See manual, automatic, and swap-triggered nudges with their outcomes, plus model changes, provider controls, hosting, cooling, and related settings actions. - Interrupted attempts remain visible after an app restart. Skipped automatic nudges record a reason without filling history on every telemetry poll. - Reported account earnings retain model, earning ID, time, token counts, and amount. These records are account-wide, may be incomplete, and do not imply a nudge caused later work. Base rewards are clearly distinguished from jobs. - History stays on this Mac, with up to 30 days or 5,000 entries. Credentials, provider keys, prompts, responses, and raw diagnostic errors are excluded. Recording failures are visible.
Action recording begins with this update; previous app actions cannot be reconstructed. Recent account earnings may be backfilled from the server's available history.
For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

# Bloomy v1.9.8
Fixes nudges getting stuck after a completed model selection change.
- Automatic and manual nudges now recognize a completed model switch as ready when the provider is otherwise fresh, idle, and serving exactly one warm model. - The automatic watcher reports why it is paused instead of misleadingly saying it is watching when the provider is not eligible. - The 15-minute idle threshold, saved key, cooldown, and daily limit remain unchanged. Active, failed, or unconfirmed switches still block nudges.
For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

# Bloomy v1.9.7
Swap now loads locally, then nudges through the network.
- Bloomy first loads and verifies the selected model on this Mac through the local API, keeping all advertised models available. - After a successful local swap, Bloomy sends one network self-route nudge using the key already saved in Nudge. The request is capped at eight output tokens, with no paid fallback. - Local loading and the network nudge have separate status messages. A missing or rejected key, unavailable model, or failed nudge does not undo a successful local swap. - The nudge is skipped if the local request fails, is canceled, cannot be confirmed, or the provider becomes busy or changes. It does not enable automatic nudging.
Enable **Hosting → Fleet + local API → This Mac only** for local swapping. Set up the existing **Nudge** key once for the network follow-up. Network nudges may reach another owned provider and do not guarantee public work.
For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

# Bloomy v1.9.6
Switch what is loaded without narrowing the models you advertise.
- **Swap** is a separate action on advertised, unloaded popup model cards. It asks this Mac to load the selected model while keeping your advertised list and saved selection unchanged. **Only** remains available when you want just one model advertised. - Swap sends one tiny request directly to the running provider’s unified local API. No cloud API key, network route, or paid fallback is used. Bloomy checks fresh local residency before reporting success. - Swap requires an idle provider with one saved model slot and one loaded model. It rechecks activity and provider identity before sending. Incoming work can subsequently load another advertised model. - If the local API is unavailable, **Open Hosting** takes you to its setup. Use unified mode bound to this Mac (127.0.0.1) and apply when ready. A standalone local server cannot change the network provider’s loaded model.
Swap uses the provider’s ordinary on-demand loading path; it does not pin residency, restart the provider, or change saved model selections.
For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

# Bloomy v1.9.5
Bloomy makes it easier to see what your Mac is doing and take action when it is quiet.
- **Manual Nudge** is now available in the dashboard toolbar and the fixed popup controls. A first-use guide links to Darkbloom's API console, explains the “my machine only” key restriction, and saves the key in macOS Keychain. Completed setup clearly confirms that manual and automatic nudges share one saved key. Replacing it is a separate action. - **Auto setup** saves all selected models with one resident model slot and one user-selected startup preload. Startup preload is explicitly enabled. Saving does not interrupt serving: Apply Live changes the advertised set, while the slot limit and startup preload take effect on the next provider start. - **Idle reminders** show Bloomy's mascot, an exclamation mark, and a steady idle label after five minutes of observed idle time. Choose Off, 5, 10, 15, or 30 minutes in Menu Bar settings. Reminders clear when work resumes or evidence is no longer fresh; they do not send requests. - **Automatic nudge** remains a separate opt-in with a 15-minute default. It now supports multiple advertised models when exactly one current model is warm, retaining the earnings checks, one-hour cooldown, and three-attempt daily limit. With several models advertised, nudges require the exact warm model ID from the self-route API; a family-only alias does not send a request. - **A steadier popup:** equal-sized model cards, a remembered Available collapse control, model refresh, and saved offline cards. GPU readings retain a clearly marked last sample when a read fails, instead of blinking away. - **Usable cooling controls:** corrected fan freshness handling, visible Refresh readings actions, and stable refresh labels in Settings and the popup Cooling panel.
Nudges send one exclusive self-route request capped at eight output tokens, with no paid fallback. They do not guarantee public jobs, and a self-route response may come from another owned Mac. Existing keys, preferences, history, and provider settings are preserved. iPhone companion support remains in development.
For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer.

# Bloomy v1.9.4
The macOS menu-bar companion formerly called Darkbloom Control is now **Bloomy**. It has a new compute-companion character, app icon, and menu-bar mark. The official Darkbloom provider and CLI keep their names. Existing settings, local history, bundle identity, and signed-update identity carry forward across the rename.
- **Automatic nudge**, off by default, can make a tiny request to your own warm model after 15 minutes of observed idle time (or 30 or 60 minutes). It needs a separate “my machine only” consumer key stored in the macOS Keychain and fresh account evidence showing base rewards without work. It runs only while Bloomy is open, has no paid fallback, waits at least an hour between attempts, and allows at most three attempts in 24 hours. - **Automatic profit switching**, also off by default, can change the single model this Mac advertises using Darkbloom's graceful switch. It considers only downloaded compatible models and requires fresh demand, earnings, power, memory, and idle-state evidence. After allowing for loading, the estimated next-hour net advantage must be at least **30% and $0.05** and persist for the configured confirmation period. Hold, return-wait, and loading times are configurable; attempts are capped at three per 24 hours. Existing multi-model setups are left alone. - Restored native Settings windows now show the complete settings interface. - The popup and dashboard continue to show provider health, model activity, recorded earnings, estimated electricity cost, forecasts, alerts, and explicit model and lifecycle controls. Built-in Chat offers an on-Mac destination and a separately gated paid network destination. Official fan-helper controls remain in Settings; Hosting controls are in the dashboard.
These estimates use observed account earnings and local Mac activity; account work on another machine can affect attribution. Neither watcher promises public jobs or future earnings. The independent recommendation journal remains observe-only. Remote iPhone pairing and control are still in development and are **not** included in this Mac release.
Sparkle upgrades preserve your installed app’s folder name while updating its displayed name to Bloomy. You can quit it and rename that folder to `Bloomy.app`. For a manual upgrade, quit Darkbloom Control and replace the old app with `Bloomy.app`; keep only one installed copy. The release download is for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer. The release app is Developer ID signed, notarized by Apple, stapled, and accepted by Gatekeeper.

# Darkbloom Control v1.9.3
After a confirmed **Use only this model** switch, Control sends one small test request through Darkbloom's free self-route to help load the selected model. The popup shows when the model responds and explains when the test is skipped or fails. A saved Chat API key is required; the request cannot fall back to paid fleet routing.
This is an emergency workaround for CLI switches that leave a model unloaded. A successful test confirms that an owned provider responded, but it does not guarantee that the public scheduler will send jobs. The switch itself remains successful if the test cannot run.

# Darkbloom Control v1.9.2
- Make the menu-bar popup easier to scan with three model cards per row, short model names, compact speed and earnings readings, and full names on hover. - Show advertised and locally available models separately. Available models can be added directly; a confirmed “Use only” action switches the running provider to one downloaded model after accepted work drains. - Recommend one model resident at a time in Capacity, with a startup model preference. Other enabled models can still load when requested. Saved model choices remain visible in a muted state when live provider status is absent. - Clarify whether a model is serving now, in memory, or waiting to load, and simplify the popup's fan status and controls.
The provider CLI chooses among enabled models for incoming work. This release does not add an earnings-based switching scheduler. A saved capacity change requires a provider restart; switching the advertised model does not.

# Darkbloom Control v1.9.1
- Organize the sidebar into collapsible groups and split Settings into focused pages, preserving unfinished edits when switching between Settings pages. - Simplify fan control around the official helper's on/off switch and live GPU temperature and fan readings. Keep optional policy adjustments out of the way. - Hide unused legacy Gemma catalog entries while keeping configured or running models visible and manageable. - Explain model-cache command timeouts without exposing private command output, and include the macOS external-volume usage description in packaged apps.
Fan changes still require the official helper's confirmation and administrator approval. This release does not implement custom fan curves or a replacement helper. iOS companion support remains in development for version 2.0.

# Darkbloom Control v1.9.0
- Redesign the menu-bar popup around your Mac's name, GPU utilization, fan readings and controls, and a compact two-column grid of advertised and available models. - Use shared model cards with family icons, short names, full names on hover, serving state, measured speed, and clearly labeled earnings when available. - Make Overview denser, standardize Activity filters, and reorganize Opportunity into compact comparison cards with detailed reasoning available on demand. - Let Models expand to three columns when the window has enough room. - Rework Health & Logs with clearer source status, a selectable log table, responsive filters, and full event details. - Bring earnings and estimated electricity costs together while keeping missing measurements and observation coverage explicit.
This update changes presentation without moving models or changing provider, fan, model-selection, or automatic-update preferences. The iOS companion and remote-control service remain coming soon.

# Darkbloom Control v1.8.0
- Apply a saved model selection through Darkbloom 0.9.11's graceful live switch when fresh provider state confirms that the operation is safe. The popup also explains the CLI coordinator's automatic model loading without implying that Control changes models on its own. - Add official Darkbloom fan-helper controls with bounded settings, exact executable identity checks, and the normal macOS administrator prompt. - Add System, Light, and Dark appearance modes. System remains the default and follows macOS appearance changes. - Record operational alerts locally, surface native notifications, and preview a bounded support packet that excludes credentials, prompts, responses, account identifiers, and filesystem paths. - Add an observe-only recommendation evidence journal with explainable factors, deterministic replay, and clear insufficient-evidence states. Recommendations never issue provider commands. - Improve Darkbloom 0.9.11 lifecycle presentation, including scheduled idle, startup preload, model-switch progress, retained slots, and safe timeout or forced-stop outcomes.
Coming soon: the iOS companion, remote QR pairing/control, and its persistent Mac helper. The current download does not install or enable a remote-control service.

# Darkbloom Control v1.7.0
- Organize Models into collapsible Enabled and Available groups, with narrower cards and up to two columns. Models that still need downloading are visually muted. - Add an independent daily-runtime slider to each model card. Forecasts are what-if estimates based on observed activity and configured electricity cost; they do not schedule or change provider runtime. Earnings inputs are account-level and assume this Mac produced the recorded work for that model. - Show whole-Mac GPU utilization as a menu-bar ring, with temperature coloring when fresh readings are available. Missing or stale utilization omits the ring; missing temperature uses a neutral color. - Share GPU sampling between the menu bar and dashboard to avoid duplicate polling.
Coming soon: the iOS companion and remote pairing/control. Fan controls, richer statistics, and automatic model warming also remain planned and are not enabled in this release.

# Darkbloom Control v1.6.0
- Add Chat inside the dashboard and in a separate resizable window. Both views share one in-memory conversation; prompts and replies are discarded on quit. - Make the destination explicit for each new conversation. Local hosting is the default. If the local endpoint is unavailable, sending stays disabled until you choose another destination; chat never switches to the paid network on its own. - Add an opt-in Darkbloom network route with a clear paid-inference warning, consumer balance and pricing information, and a fresh balance check before each send. The network can still reject a request when credits are insufficient. The consumer API key is stored in the macOS Keychain. - Add local hosting controls for loopback or LAN access, model selection, and optional endpoint bearer authentication. Chat also supports a local endpoint intentionally configured without a bearer token. - Keep beta review builds separate from the installed app's preferences, history, and single-instance lock so they can run side by side.

# Darkbloom Control v1.5.0
- Show best-effort, whole-Mac GPU utilization in the provider resources panel, alongside the provider's reported GPU memory. - Show provider request activity: `1+` while inference is active and the exact accepted requests remaining during a graceful drain. - Use the CLI's native graceful-stop behavior to pause new admissions and drain accepted work, replacing the app's former idle-polling stop flow. - Keep the Models window within the visible screen area with a compact toolbar and responsive, enabled-first model cards.

# Darkbloom Control v1.4.2
- Give the Models dashboard a larger, screen-aware window so the card grid is easier to read at normal size. - Show up to three model cards across and two rows at once, with additional models available by scrolling. - Reduce space above the cards with a collapsed selection summary and compact search field beside the section picker. - Sort enabled models first while preserving the existing order within each enabled or disabled group.

# Darkbloom Control v1.4.1
- Refine model cards with larger, centered metric icons and overlapping values. - Explain card metrics, network demand, request counts, opportunity grades, and staged enable/preload controls on hover. - Add active and waiting network request counts next to demand and replace the demand bars with a shaded, color-coded shield. - Put enable and load-at-startup switches on each downloaded model card, remove the redundant catalog RAM requirement from the card face, and keep forecasts and detailed compatibility information in Manage & Forecast. - Keep card sizing uniform and readable, with at most four columns.

# Darkbloom Control v1.4.0
- Replace the model list with responsive, branded cards showing measured speed, live demand, average net profit per active hour, local opportunity grade, and catalog hardware fit. - Add per-model daily compute-allocation scenarios with a shared 24-hour budget. Projections extrapolate from measured serving activity and clearly separate estimated gross payout from incremental whole-Mac adapter power cost. - Require at least two hours of observed active serving before showing a model's profit projection; serving allocation estimates compute time and is separate from the number of models resident in memory.

# Darkbloom Control v1.3.1
- Fix a crash when filtering Activity charts by clicking a model pill. - Align Activity controls and keep model names readable across window sizes.
